transport: CAN over RJ45 (CAN IN / CAN OUT) on Cat5/Cat6 straight-through patch cable · 120 Ω terminator plug at each end of the bus · the same RJ45 carries two separate buses, CAN BUS (inverter/charger messaging) and STK BUS (stacking) · extended 29-bit arbitration IDs, message id = (arbitration_id >> 18) & 0x7FF · bit rate NOT published by MidNite and not stated by the one community decoder · RJ45 pin-to-C
blocks: No register map exists. The bus is message-oriented, and the only published id list is one community decoder's: 0x040 AC output voltage · 0x041 AC output watts · 0x101 AC input volts/amps/Hz · 0x102 AC input watts · 0x2A4 battery temperature · 0x331 and 0x261 FET + transformer temperature. System-wide frames shared with MidNite charge controllers on the same bus: 0xA0 battery V/A/W · 0xA3 charge stage · 0x2A3 WhizBang Jr. amps · 0x022 daily kWh · 0x81 PV voltage.

You cannot make the tap cable from the manual. MidNite documents the CAN connectors as RJ45 CAN IN / CAN OUT with Cat5/Cat6 straight-through and a terminator plug, but publishes no pin-to-CAN-H/CAN-L assignment. The only pinout in circulation is a PDF ("SA cable1.pdf") posted by the MidNite forum admin on midniteftp.co

The RJ45 carries two buses. Per 10-607-1 Rev B (3-Phase Stacking), the Rosie cable has a CAN BUS section for inverter/charger messaging and an STK BUS section for stacking messaging, terminated independently — CAN by a plug at each end, STK by a jumper on the front-panel PCBA (shipped on TERM). unmappedReports: AC INPUT voltage / current / frequency / power, distinct from AC output. The Rosie is an inverter/charger with a 60 A transfer relay, so frames 0x101 and 0x102 (input) and 0x040/0x041 (output) are live at the same time. MetricKind has only one set of ac-voltage / ac-current / ac-frequency / ac-power. Two devices reporting into the same wire names, or a contract variant, is a real decision this dialect forces., Inverter power-FET heatsink temperature (0x331/0x261 byte 0-1). Nearest wire name is the generic `temperature`, which the contract documents as an environment reading. The EPEver driver hit the same wall — cabin-epever notes 0x3111 is "the temperature inside the controller, not the room"., Transformer temperature (0x331/0x261 byte 2-3). Same problem, and it is a second internal temperature on the same device, so one `temperature` slot cannot carry both., ChargeStage cannot express what the bus sends. The community decoder's table is 0 Resting, 1 Bulk MPPT, 2 Absorb, 3 Float, 4 Equalize, 5 Float MPPT, 6 EQ MPPT. `ChargeStage` has idle/bulk/absorption/float/equalize/fault/unknown, so 5 and 6 collapse onto float and equalize and the MPPT-vs-not distinction is lost. This is a ValueKind finding, not a MetricKind one., AUX relay state. The Rosie has programmable AUX terminals (manual p.26/p.45) driving an external relay. Nothing on the decoded bus carries it, and `switch-state` would be the wire name if it did., Auto Gen Start state. The MNGP2 has an Auto GEN Start menu with setpoints, so a Rosie installation may already be starting the generator on its own. Nothing decoded reports it, and `generator-run-state` would be the wire name.
